I fixed the `IndexError` in `is_mostly_bin` (`mitmproxy/utils/strutils.py`) and added a test. I haven't run the tests.

**Cause:** for inputs longer than 100 bytes, the function checks bytes 100–103 to avoid cutting a UTF-8 character in half. With 101–103 bytes of data, `s[cut]` ran past the end of the input.

**Fix:** the continuation-byte check is now `cut < len(s) and (s[cut] >> 6) == 0b10`. When `cut` reaches the end of the data, nothing can be split, so it counts as a boundary and the whole input is kept. Inputs of 100 bytes or fewer, and inputs of 104 bytes or more, take exactly the same path as before, so their results don't change.

**Test:** in `test_is_mostly_bin` (`test/mitmproxy/utils/test_strutils.py`), I added a loop over lengths 101–104. It asserts that `n * b"a"` is not binary and `n * b"\x00"` is binary.
